title: Every geometric inverse image has these algebraic lifts and canonical constant maps.
statement: Let C and C' be small categories in a common universe with Grothendieck topologies J and J'. Let L : Sheaf J (Type u) ⥤ Sheaf J' (Type u) and V : Sheaf J' (Type u) ⥤ Sheaf J (Type u) with an adjunction L ⊣ V, and assume PreservesFiniteLimits L. Then Nonempty (InverseImageData L), where InverseImageData L consists of: a functor rings : Sheaf J CommRingCat → Sheaf J' CommRingCat; for every commutative-ring sheaf O on J, an AlgebraicInverseImage L O (rings.obj O), including its ringUnderlying and moduleUnderlying comparisons and the transported ring/module operation graph equations; a naturality equation for every ring morphism φ : R ⟶ S, namely L.map (forget.map φ) ≫ (algebra S).ringUnderlying.hom = (algebra R).ringUnderlying.hom ≫ forget.map (rings.map φ); and a natural isomorphism constants : constantSheaf J CommRingCat ⋙ rings ≅ constantSheaf J' CommRingCat. The constants component at each ring is the canonical constant-sheaf map, and all maps are natural in coefficient-ring morphisms.

proof.text: Apply lem-route-inverse-image-ring-functor to obtain rings and, for each source ring sheaf, its underlying comparison e_R and the ring-operation transport.

For each O, apply lem-route-inverse-image-module-lift to R = O, A = rings.obj O and the isomorphism e_O of Step 1, whose identification of addition, multiplication, zero and one is the hypothesis of that node. This supplies (algebra O) with ringUnderlying exactly e_O, the moduleUnderlying comparison, and every ring/module graph equation required by the AlgebraicInverseImage field.

For a ring morphism φ : R ⟶ S, Step 2 gives (algebra R).ringUnderlying = e_R and (algebra S).ringUnderlying = e_S, and the naturality clause of lem-route-inverse-image-ring-functor, e_S ∘ L(|φ|) = |rings φ| ∘ e_R, is exactly the displayed ring_naturality equation after writing the two underlying-set functors as sheafCompose (forget CommRingCat).

Apply lem-route-inverse-image-constant-comparison to rings and the natural family e of Step 1 (natural, and compatible with the ring operations, by lem-route-inverse-image-ring-functor) to obtain the natural constants isomorphism; its components are the canonical constant-sheaf maps and are natural in coefficient morphisms.
Package rings, the family algebra, ring_naturality, and constants into the InverseImageData record. The result is an inhabitant, hence its type is Nonempty (InverseImageData L).
